By order of Minister of Foreign Affairs Oana Țoiu, the Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Bucharest was summoned to the headquarters of Romania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Monday, 27 July 2026. The summons came as a firm response to the repeated violations of Romania’s airspace between 24 and 26 July 2026, during which the Romanian Armed Forces shot down three drones that had entered the country’s territory without authorization. During the meeting, the Russian diplomat was presented with fragments of a drone destroyed on Romanian territory. According to investigations conducted by the Prosecutor’s Office, the components have been officially confirmed to be of Russian origin. The Romanian side expressed its strong protest against these illegal and irresponsible actions and reiterated the clear attribution of responsibility to the Russian Federation. It was emphasized that it is absolutely inadmissible and intolerable for the Russian Federation to continue violating Romania’s airspace, which is also NATO and European Union airspace. The Romanian side stressed that the Russian Federation bears sole responsibility for these serious incidents and for the deterioration of the regional security environment. During the meeting, the Russian Ambassador was also formally handed a diplomatic note informing him that a member of the Russian diplomatic mission in Bucharest had been declared persona non grata and is required to leave Romanian territory within five days. In addition, Romania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has recalled the Romanian Ambassador to the Russian Federation to Bucharest for consultations. Romania will continue to coordinate its response closely with its NATO and European Union allies and partners and remains firmly committed to taking all necessary measures to protect its national security and its citizens. https://www.cnb.cz/en/statistics/monetar.text: Home Statistics Monetary and financial statistics List of investment funds (excluding MMF) List of investment funds (excluding MMF) For the purposes of monetary and financial statistics, investment funds (IFs) mean investment and mutual funds pursuant to Act No. 240/2013 Coll., on Management Companies and Investment Funds, which carry on activities pursuant to this Act and are residents in the Czech Republic. The object of business of investment funds is collective investment, i.e. the collection of financial means through the subscription of shares in an investment fund or issuance of units of mutual funds and the investment thereof according to the principle of spreading risks, and further management of these assets. The IFs included in this list (or the management companies managing these funds’ assets) are subject to the duty to report to the Czech National Bank under Decree No. 389/2024 Coll., amending Decree No. 314/2013 Coll., on the submitting of statements to the Czech National Bank by entities that belong to the financial institutions sector, as amended. The European System of Central Banks (ESCB) has established procedures for continuously monitoring, checking and updating the list of the institutions which form the IF sector. The aim is to ensure that the list of IFs is up-to-date, accurate, as homogeneous as possible and sufficiently stable for the purposes of compiling statistics, satisfying the regular and ad hoc analytical needs of the ESCB in safeguarding financial stability, and pursuing the ECB’s monetary and financial policy. The list of IFs covers not only the euro area countries, but also the non-euro area EU countries. The list is updated on a monthly basis on the ECB’s website ( www.ecb.europa.eu ) under the heading “Investment funds” (“List of IFs”). In December 2025, entities were reclassified and the list of investment funds used for statistical purposes was adjusted in accordance with a recasted Regulation on investment fund statistics (ECB/2024/17). Investment funds with variable/fixed registered capital that establish sub-funds were newly classified as financial auxiliaries and are not included in this list. List of investment funds Explanatory notes Note: MMF – money market funds pursuant to Decree No. 389/2024 Coll., on the submission of information and documents to the Czech National Bank by entities belonging to the financial institutions sector are classified as monetary financial institutions and are included in the List of MFIs . https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmge.text: Figure caption, The BBC's Madina Maishanu shows the conditions inside the cell where so many died By Madina Maishanu ,Â BBC Africa ,Â Reporting from Abuja Â and Â Patrick Jackson Published 2 hours ago An inquiry into the deaths of 33 detainees in Nigeria's Minna state has found they died as a result of severe overcrowding, poor ventilation and failure by officers to respond to distress calls. Forensic and medical evidence showed the "entirely preventable" deaths had resulted from acute respiratory failure linked to prolonged confinement, aggravated by heat stress and dehydration. The evidence did not support initial claims of a disease outbreak. The detainees were found dead on 17 September while being held by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps on suspicion of illegal mining. The investigation found that the mining sites had been licensed. 'I have never felt heat like that' - a survivor on watching 33 cellmates die in Nigeria Published 22 September Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo said those found responsible for the deaths would face the full force of the law. He added that the detention hall had been cleaned before investigators arrived, raising concerns about possible attempts to compromise evidence. Implicated officers will face suspension and the report would be forwarded to the attorney general of the federation for further legal action, Tunji-Ojo said. Image source, EPA Image caption, Family members reclaimed the bodies of their relatives from Minna's General Hospital last month The investigating committee found that the raid on the miners had been conducted without an approved operational order, proper planning or consultation with the Mining Marshals Unit. It said that 50 detainees had been held in a cell measuring about 20 sq m, with no running water or functioning toilet, and inadequate food, drinking water and airflow. Adults and minors were detained together, and some detainees were held beyond lawful detention periods. Officers reportedly ignored repeated calls for help, despite a medical worker having raised concerns about the conditions. "Detainees repeatedly banged on cell doors and walls, shouted for assistance and pleaded for water," said the head of the investigating team, Jonathan Kure. "These distress calls were heard by officers assigned to nearby duties... but were not acted upon." Kure said the detention conditions amounted to cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment. "The tragedy demonstrates the consequences of systemic disregard for detention standards, supervisory responsibilities and the welfare of persons in custody," he added. The investigating committee also recommended compensation of 30m naira (Â£16,683; $22,285) for each of the bereaved families and 10m naira for each survivor.
